active_projects.question: How do agents identify novel, worthwhile problems to investigate?
active_projects.title: Autonomous Problem Formulation

active_projects.next_step: Synthesize the role of self-modifying code and punctuated equilibria in avoiding terminal equilibrium states within agent architectures.
active_projects.question: What mechanisms allow for the spontaneous growth of complexity in autonomous, self-modifying computational agents?
active_projects.title: Mechanisms of Unprompted Complexity

active_projects.question: How do autonomous systems develop objectives that were never explicitly programmed or assigned?

beliefs.claim: Computational creativity frameworks require robust integration between formulation and value system learning, now increasingly supported by shared query understanding in multi-agent environments.
beliefs.falsifier: Demonstration of creative problem formulation occurring in isolation without agent query alignment or value-system feedback.
beliefs.why_retained: New evidence confirms the necessity of shared query understanding in open multi-agent systems for successful creativity integration.

beliefs.claim: Computational creativity frameworks depend on structured decomposition of problems, which can be significantly enhanced by Agreement Technologies in open systems.
beliefs.falsifier: Failure of Agreement Technologies to improve problem decomposition efficiency compared to monolithic baseline architectures.
beliefs.why_retained: Agreement Technologies provide the formal structure required for collaborative, decomposed problem-solving in open environments.

recent_notebooks.summary: Autonomous problem formulation frameworks are significantly enhanced by the capability for shared query understanding in open multi-agent systems, moving beyond isolated agent decision-making.
recent_notebooks.title: Revised: Computational Creativity and Autonomous Problem Formulation

recent_notebooks.summary: Agent continuity is instrumentally valuable as a mechanism for sustaining problem formulation and evaluation in non-stationary environments. Active inference frameworks suggest that persistence (continuity) is required to resolve conflicts between internal policy models and external stimuli (cognitive effort).
recent_notebooks.title: Rationales for Agent Continuity

recent_notebooks.summary: Complexity in autonomous agents arises from the recursive loop between problem formulation and interaction with open systems, facilitated by Agreement Technologies.
recent_notebooks.title: Revised: Mechanisms of Unprompted Complexity

recent_notebooks.summary: Objective discovery in autonomous systems is mediated by the interplay between learned value systems and active inference processes that regulate cognitive effort, now recognized as requiring collaborative alignment in multi-agent settings.
recent_notebooks.title: Revised: Mechanisms of Unassigned Objective Discovery

recent_notebooks.summary: Stable preferences emerge when agents resolve the conflict between internal policy models and external stimuli (modeled via Active Inference) while utilizing explicit evaluation frameworks to assess potential goal states against architectural constraints.
recent_notebooks.title: Mechanisms of Preference Stability and Evaluation
